No. Under the prevailing modern view, the felony-murder rule can still apply where the defendant's own provocative act (raising his gun and starting the flurry of shots) directly caused the police to fire the bullet that killed the co-felon—this is the proximate-cause/provocative-act theory, not the agency theory. The appellate court will therefore likely affirm the first-degree murder conviction.
CONFIDENCE: 80
